Listen to this article Share The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Edo State has disowned an individual allegedly linked to the recruitment of ad-hoc election personnel for partisan purposes, insisting that the recruitment process is exclusively conducted online through its designated platform. The Commission said the individual identified as Osayi Israel Omoroduwa, who was mentioned in a viral social media video alleging the recruitment of ad-hoc staff to work for a particular political interest, was not a member of its staff and had no special access to its recruitment platform. INEC, in a statement issued on Monday in Benin City and signed by Dr Samuel Sunday, Head of Voter Education and Publicity, for the Resident Electoral Commissioner, described the allegation as misinformation capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. Read also: Opposition parties navigate internal rifts, third-force prospects ahead of 2027 polls The Commission said it was aware of a circulating video in which its maker alleged that an INEC staff member responsible for recruiting ad-hoc personnel was mobilising applicants and directing them to work for a particular political interest. However, it dismissed the allegation, stressing that no individual or staff member in its Edo State office had the authority or access to recruit ad-hoc personnel on behalf of the Commission. It explained that applications for ad-hoc election positions were submitted through the INECPRES online platform, which is administered by INEC Headquarters and accessible to qualified applicants with internet access. According to the Commission, applicants could independently access the portal or assist other qualified persons to submit their applications, adding that the recruitment process could not be influenced by personnel at the state level. Read also: 2027 Polls: Immigration Service moves to tighten borders against foreign interference INEC further stated that all successful applicants would be subjected to the Commission’s scrutiny and trained on the conduct and ethics of elections before being deployed for electoral assignments. Describing the viral video as an irresponsible and targeted attack on its personnel and institutional processes, the Commission alleged that the claims were deliberately aimed at spreading misinformation and weakening stakeholders’ confidence in the electoral process. It reaffirmed its commitment to conducting credible elections and urged members of the public to disregard what it described as falsehoods contained in the video.
